transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2027-01-19
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sam Carter (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood CSM), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Lena Zhou (Redwood Support); Jordan Lee (Acme Head of ML), Priya Singh (Platform Lead), Tom Alvarez (DevOps), Hannah Park (Security)

---
Summary: Quick kickoff to align on onboarding milestones, security review items, and pilot plan. Some transcription artifacts present.

00:00 Sam Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, i'm Sam Carter, i'm the AE on the account. with me is maya our CSM, diego on SE and lena on support. jordan, priya, tom, hannah, thanks for making time.
00:18 Jordan Lee: Thanks Sam, excited to get started. quick context -- we're running inference for clinical triage models, low latency needs for chat experiences and embeddings for search.
00:30 Priya Singh: yeah we host in us-west, mostly k8s on EKS, some on-prem for PHI. curious about private deployment options.
00:40 Maya Patel: great. high level we typically do: network checklist, SSO and RBAC, pilot with a dedicated pool if needed, and a week of benchmarks. we'll tailor for PHI requirements.
00:58 Tom Alvarez: question on VPC peering — do you support cross-account VPC peering or Transit Gateway? we have strict firewall rules.
01:08 Diego Ruiz: we support VPC peering and transit gateway patterns; for private customers we can do customer-managed VPC with control plane access restricted. port list is pretty small, we'll send the exact ports. note there is TLS and mTLS options for control plane.
01:30 Hannah Park: on security, SOC2 is critical for us, also we need KMS integration, CMEK, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. is that all possible?
01:42 Maya Patel: yes SOC2 report available, we support KMS/HSM and CMEK for private deployments, and audit logs export to common formats. i'll attach the security pack after this call.
01:54 Jordan Lee: great. one of our constraints is latency. we have 95th p99 latency SLO of 250 ms for short text generation under 1k tokens. curious whether hosted will meet that or if we need Dedicated.
02:10 Diego Ruiz: latency is workload dependent. for short sequences and higher qps, Dedicated GPU pools with pinned capacity are most reliable; hosted can work in many cases but burstiness and noisy neighbors can push p99 up. we also do KV cache and prefix caching to bring down tail latency.
02:30 Sam Carter: pricing-wise dedicated is commit-based; we'll share tiers. for pilots we usually offer a short committed window or a smaller dedicated pool plus host fallback.
02:45 Priya Singh: can you explain the model variants and fallback? we want graceful degradation if we lose capacity.
02:52 Diego Ruiz: yes, we route by policy. you can set latency or cost-first routing and provide compatible model variants — e.g., quantized 7B fallback. that keeps availability up while controlling cost. sometimes the transcript spells it as 'K V cahce' but it's KV cache.
03:12 Jordan Lee: perfect. also need to validate data residency — some datasets must remain in region. do you support region pinning?
03:20 Maya Patel: yes region pinning available for Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted has regional endpoints and we'll ensure data residency controls.
03:30 Tom Alvarez: network wise, whats the expected egress IP list? we need to put rules in firewall.
03:36 Diego Ruiz: we'll provide static egress IPs for the private connector and peering endpoints; host endpoints vary unless you use dedicated/private. we'll send a one-pager.
03:48 Hannah Park: about SSO and provisioning: SAML? SCIM? role-based access?
03:55 Maya Patel: SAML SSO supported, SCIM provisioning for users, and RBAC with role templates. for enterprise we do SCIM + SAML, and you can map SAML groups to roles.
04:08 Jordan Lee: great. timeline — what's the typical onboarding cadence?
04:12 Sam Carter: usually 2-4 weeks for basic hosted integration; Dedicated/private can be 4-8 weeks depending on network & security approvals. first week: network and SSO, second: pilot traffic and benchmarking, third: validation & runbooks, fourth: go-live prep.
04:30 Priya Singh: for pilot, what metrics should we measure? latency P50/P95/P99, CPU/GPU utilization, token cost per million, and end-to-end error rates?
04:40 Diego Ruiz: exactly. also memory/KV cache hit rates and model quality checks. we'll run a benchmark harness.
04:52 Jordan Lee: about model onboarding: do you host our proprietary fine-tuned weights or do we bring our own?
05:00 Diego Ruiz: both. we can host customer models in private deployments or dedicated pools; for hosted you can upload weights with RBAC and optional encryption at rest. we'll walk through model pinning and rollouts.
05:15 Tom Alvarez: who has access to keys? we need proof that Redwood doesn't have access to CMEK keys.
05:20 Maya Patel: CMEK is customer-managed, Redwood can't read keys. we'll provide key rotation docs.
05:28 Priya Singh: any gotchas for k8s integrations? we're trying to keep things simple.
05:33 Diego Ruiz: not many, mostly service account configs and routing. if using our private on-prem package there is an agent; for VPC we do connector + service endpoints. we'll share a k8s quickstart.
05:50 Jordan Lee: ok good. next procedural Q: support SLAs and escalation path?
05:55 Maya Patel: for enterprise we provide an SLA tied to Dedicated, include 24/7 support for Sev1, with a named CSM and escalation to SRE. support runbooks live in the console.
06:08 Sam Carter: i'll follow up with contract language and pilot pricing.
06:12 Priya Singh: worked examples of cost savings via caching and batching would help sell to finance.
06:18 Diego Ruiz: we have a cost model spreadsheet and recommendations like quantization profiles, batching params and cache TTLs that show unit economics. we'll share that link.
06:30 Jordan Lee: any security questionnaire examples? we're doing a vendor security review next week.
06:36 Maya Patel: yes we have an information security questionnaire (SIG) and filled SAML/SCIM samples. i'll attach to the pack.
06:45 Tom Alvarez: can we schedule network deep-dive next week, ideally with our infra and network security folks?
06:50 Sam Carter: absolutely. diego, can you host that?
06:52 Diego Ruiz: yes I'll run the checklist. propose Tuesday 2027-01-26 at 10am PT.
06:58 Jordan Lee: that works.
07:01 Maya Patel: recap of next steps: maya sends security pack and SOC2, sam sends pricing, diego sends port list and network checklist, jordan uploads traffic traces. we'll schedule network meeting and a benchmark week.
07:15 Jordan Lee: sounds good. thanks everyone. looking forward.
07:20 Sam Carter: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.
07:25 Lena Zhou: if anyone hits issues with the shared folder i'll help.
07:28 Priya Singh: thanks.
07:30 Meeting end.
